newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish central bank moves to sell two banks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Polish central bank moves to sell two banks - paper.

text.p: Poland's central bank has set a September 23 deadline for final bids in the planned joint privatisation of two banks it controls, the Polish Investment Bank (PBI) and Prosper SA, the bank's deputy head said.

"By this deadline (investors) have to submit price offers and I think we should be able to begin negotiations a week later," Witold Kozinski, deputy president of the National Bank of Poland (NBP), told Nowa Europa.
The daily's Wednesday edition quoted him as saying he was confident the two banks would be sold by the end of 1996.
"We have a selected group of investors. Half of them are foreign institutions and half are domestic," Kozinski said.

He said that talks with one foreign investor on privatisation of Pierwszy Komercyjny Bank w Lublinie, another bank supervised by the NBP, had recently stalled but there were other institutions showing interest.
PBI, carved out of the NBP in 1993 with a clean credit portfolio, remains 100-percent owned by the central bank and reported a net profit of 44 million zlotys in 1995.
The NBP took control of more than 90 percent of ailing Prosper Bank in 1993 as a result of a bail-out scheme and has since retained its stake to guide the bank's turnaround.
